newsitem.title: UK: Burmah shows strength in falling FTSE 100.
newsitem.headline: Burmah shows strength in falling FTSE 100.

text.p: Shares in Burmah Castrol Plc rose on Wednesday, in sharp contrast to a tumbling FTSE 100 index, as traders tried to cover short positions and crude oil prices dropped slightly, analysts said.
At 1205 GMT Burmah was up 25p at 10.88-1/2 stg. The FTSE 1000 index was down 47.8 points to 3987.9 points at the time.
"Some marketmakers are short of stock and so they're frantically looking to buy, which is pushing the price up," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
Added Jurjen Lunshof, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing: "We may see it push through 11.00 stg as quite a few people are bidding for the stock."
"Burmah is always pushed up on the back of a falling oil price," Lunshof said. "The Burmah bulls will decide to role out their cause on that basis," he said.
He added that Burmah had underperformed the UK oil sector over the past year.
At 1104 GMT January Brent was trading 24 cents off at $23.05 a barrel. It had been pushed below $23.00 at the open.
